title: Unknown JSON keys are silently ignored instead of rejected
evidence: src/books.c:137-148 parse_book maps only title/author/isbn/year; any other key is parsed and dropped with no error
suggestion: Optionally reject unrecognized keys with 400 to catch client typos; harmless but lenient

title: year parsed via strtod then cast to long can overflow silently
evidence: src/books.c:129-131 uses strtod and rejects only non-integral values (d != (long)d); an out-of-range numeric year casts to long with implementation-defined result
suggestion: Use strtol with ERANGE checking, or bound the year range

title: PUT uses full-replace semantics with the same required-field validation as POST
evidence: src/books.c:271-291 update_book requires title and author (blank check) and rewrites all columns
suggestion: Reasonable REST PUT interpretation; noted for cross-run comparison (some runs implement PATCH-style partial update)

title: Tests are compiled and run under AddressSanitizer + UBSan
evidence: Makefile:12 test target adds -fsanitize=address,undefined; _agent_stdout.log shows '30 checks, 0 failures' with no sanitizer diagnostics
suggestion: Strong memory-safety signal for a hand-written C server; no action needed
